author: Tampa Bay Times
title: 'Complete disgrace' and 'total jerk': What Fauci said about DeSantis in his diary - NewsBreak
text:
5 hours ago Dr. Anthony Fauci, the former Director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, is testifying after Senator Rand Paul, Republican from Kentucky, released more than 1000 pages of Fauci's diary entries from the COVID-19 pandemic. [ ALEX WROBLEWSKI/AFP | TNS ] An hour before Dr. Anthony Fauci, the chief scientist who guided the nation through the challenges of COVID-19, stepped forward to testify before congressional leaders about his role during the pandemic — which led to the country shutting down and most people wearing masks — one of his most passionate critics, Gov. Ron DeSantis, took to social media to call the whole situation a “typical performative DC spectacle” that would result in no accountability.
DeSantis has highlighted Florida’s defiance of federal mandates for social distancing, restaurant closures and mask-wearing during the pandemic as a symbol of strong state independence and resistance to elite influence from Washington, D.C. Almost 6 years later, he continues to criticize Fauci’s pandemic-era scientific advice and recommendations.
Before Wednesday’s Senate hearing, where Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment rights, Kentucky Senator Rand Paul—who has questioned the infectious disease expert about the origins of COVID-19—released more than 1,000 pages of Fauci’s private writings. The diary entries offer a glimpse into Fauci’s thoughts on DeSantis — a “jerk,” a “disgrace” and a henchman out to get him.
But their relationship didn’t begin so adversarially, according to Fauci’s journal entries.
The diary first mentions the two men talking in early March 2020, after Fauci had incorrectly said Florida had a community spread of the virus when, in fact, it was just a cluster. According to the entry, the call was arranged by the White House after DeSantis complained.
“He was correct,” Fauci wrote on March 10, 2020. “Was nice on the phone call…We came out with a statement correcting.”
The following month, the number of cases in the United States had drastically increased. There was growing concern about the implications the virus would have for the economy. Some schools and businesses were closed across the country.
On April 10, 2020, Fauci wrote that a reporter had asked President Donald Trump about DeSantis’ plan to reopen certain schools in Florida by May, and Trump had not answered, so the reporter pivoted the question to him.
“I spoke generically, saying I am not aware of the situation in Florida, but in general, if there are active cases in the community, children in school could spread the virus,” he wrote.
Later that afternoon, he received a call from DeSantis, who told him the decision to reopen schools was being made on a week-by-week basis “and did not make any definitive decisions and the districts that he was considering opening the schools were districts with very few infections.”
According to the entries, by the fall of 2020, Fauci was holding weekly meetings with Miami mayors, including then-Miami-Dade County Mayor Carlos Gimenez and former City of Miami Mayor Francis Suarez.
In October 2020, Fauci described the mayors as being “frustrated” with DeSantis’ policies. According to the entry, the mayors had begun seeing an uptick in the number of COVID-19 cases among people 30-40 and testing was also being decreased. Fauci thought the number of cases “might not be reflective of what is going on.”
“Gov. DeSantis is legally preventing the Mayors from doing what needs to be done,” he wrote. “They cannot close bars or restaurants. DeSantis is preventing them from doing what needs to be done.”
In an entry on Nov. 19, 2020, Fauci, who had become frustrated with DeSantis, wrote that Miami’s mayors were trying to stop the virus from spreading but their hands were tied by the governor.
He said the “real problem is that the Mayors want to do the correct thing, but the Governor has ordered that bars and restaurants open at full capacity. The best that he will give the Mayors is a 2 hour curfew, i.e. close bars at 10:00 PM.”
“He is a Trumper and a real problem. Screw people dying; save the economy,” Fauci wrote of DeSantis.
Gimenez, now a Republican U.S. representative serving the Miami area in Congress, disputed Fauci’s characterization of the meetings in a statement Wednesday. He said he “had no issues with the policies of Governor DeSantis,” and that throughout that time they had “maintained a very strong working relationship.”
Suarez told the Herald Wednesday that he was looking out for the best for the city during his dealings with Fauci, and said he had “expressed frustration with the CDC.”
After a Dec. 1, 2020, call with the mayors, Fauci wrote: “still remaining issue that Governor DeSantis is blocking the mayors attempts to mitigate.”
By the summer of 2021, the relationship between the two men had become totally sour. DeSantis had created drink Koozies and t-shirts that read “Don’t Fauci My Florida.”
“Gov. DeSantis has made anti-Fauci T-shirts. Amazing!!,” Fauci wrote on July 17, 2021.
Fauci grew even more critical of DeSantis’ handling of the COVID-19 virus in Florida. In his August diary, he called DeSantis a “total jerk” who was “causing people to die in his home state.”
“Governor DeSantis is a complete disgrace,” he wrote.
Fauci said DeSantis had joined the “Greek chorus” of Rand Paul, other Republican members of Congress and the “stooges at Fox News” to actively criticize him and have him fired. He became convinced that the attacks on him were also tied to the denial of the 2020 elections and the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol, which he called “The Big Lie.”
“This is an obviously calculated plan of disparaging me and any other scientists (but focusing heavily on me) that speak up against their crazy strategy,” he wrote.
In December 2022, after more than 38 years, Fauci stepped down from his leadership role at the National Institutes of Health. The ceremony was how he liked it, he wrote in a Dec. 16 entry — “no bells and whistles.”
In the last entry in the released documents, dated Dec. 17, DeSantis was still on his mind.
“It is clear (I have not been reporting it every day) that the far, extreme right and Qanon literally hate me,” he wrote. “And DeSantis is starting to play into this with his growing campaign for presidency.”
DeSantis’ campaign for president failed. But he rallied many Republicans and COVID-19 skeptics to his camp.
During Wednesday’s hearing before the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, Florida Republican Senator Ashley Moody scolded Fauci for his choice of words in describing DeSantis and for saying the United States’ democracy was in “dire danger” because “they were fighting back for the truth” from the government.
After the hearing, Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier, a DeSantis acolyte, said on social media he was launching an investigation into the infectious disease scientist.
“It’s past time we get the truth of what happened during COVID,” he said.
